Title: Sucker Spawn
Body (HTML):
Loops of angora or knitting yarn imitating the 2 to 3 mm pale-yellow egg clusters of white suckers and redhorse, which spawn late April into late May (peak around May 10 in the Detroit River study) on the same gravel trout and drop-back steelhead use. Fish it #10 to #14 under an indicator directly below sucker redds; the U.P. window runs into June.

Fish it for: Steelhead, Brown trout, Rainbow trout (resident)

Title: Black Stonefly Nymph

Chuck Hawkins ties it large during spring runoff.

Title: Zoo Cougar
Body (HTML):
Developed by Kelly Galloup in the mid 1990s for the Manistee, a neutrally buoyant deer-hair sculpin that dives and darts on a sink tip. The original is a mellow sulphur yellow; Galloup's rotation runs white, black, tan, olive, yellow and chartreuse, with light colors on bright days, olive or gray under clouds and tan when the river 'turns yellow' in late afternoon. Fish #2 to #4 hardest in April and May and late September through November, and #6 through summer at dawn and dusk.

Fish it for: Brown trout, Rainbow trout (resident), Brook trout, Steelhead

Kelly Galloup, Manistee River (Troutsman fly shop), mid-1990s
